entities.name: PMID:35111136
observations: Mouse maternal high-fat-diet model assessed male F1 beta-cell fraction and later glucose tolerance.

entities.name: Male F1 islet remodeling
observations: In mice, maternal preconception and developmental high-fat diet was followed by male F1 islet hypertrophy, increased alpha- and beta-cell mass, weak Pdx1 staining, hyperinsulinemia, fasting hyperglycemia, and glucose intolerance at 3 months.

entities.name: Male F2 islet remodeling
observations: In mice, male F2 offspring retained islet hypertrophy, increased alpha- and beta-cell mass, weak Pdx1 staining, and hyperinsulinemia, but did not show significant fasting hyperglycemia or glucose intolerance.

entities.name: Male F1 subclinical islet defect
observations: In mice, male F1 islets had reduced ATP-linked respiration, more uncoupled respiration, fewer docked insulin granules, altered calcium-channel gene expression, and increased cleaved caspase-3 despite comparable glucose tolerance and stimulated insulin secretion.

entities.name: Male F1 beta-cell fraction
observations: In mice, maternal high-fat diet was associated with reduced beta-cell fraction in male F1 newborns; adult males had similar chow glucose tolerance, with transient intolerance after high-fat-diet rechallenge.
